title: Fabrication of Carbon Nanotube High-Frequency Nanoelectronic Biosensor for Sensing in High Ionic Strength Solutions
protocol: Begin with a silicon wafer with a low pressure chemical vapor deposition (CVD) grown 500 nm Si3N4/ 500 nm SiO2 film on top.
Spin coat a layer of photoresist at 500 rpm for 5 sec and then 4,000 rpm for 40 sec.
Bake the wafer at 115 °C for 90 sec.
Expose the wafer in UV (365 nm) irradiance of 300 mJ/cm2 for 0.3 sec using a photomask with rectangular pits for catalysts.
After exposure, bake the wafer at 115 °C for 90 sec.
Develop the wafer in developer for 70 sec gently shaking the wafer through the process.
Rinse the wafer with DI water for 2 min and then blow dry with a nitrogen (N2) gun.
Load the developed wafer into e-beam evaporator chamber and deposit 0.5 nm iron (Fe) at a chamber pressure of 10-6 torr.
Dice the wafer into smaller dies 1.5 cm x 1.5 cm.
Remove the photoresist by dipping in warm acetone and isopropanol (IPA) for 10 min each.
Place the catalyst coated dies in the quartz tube of the CVD growth furnace.
Anneal the substrate in air at 880 °C for one hour to remove photoresist residue.
Purge the chamber with Argon for 5 min at 3 SLM.
Ramp up the furnace to 800 °C while maintaining a flow of 1 SLM of argon.
Flow 0.2 SLM of hydrogen for 5 min to reduce catalyst particles.
Introduce 5.5 sccm of ethylene for 35 min to grow SWNTs.
Maintain a H2 flow of 0.2 SLM throughout the process.
Allow the furnace to cool down to room temperature with a small argon flow.
Design a photomask for defining source-drain electrodes for current-voltage characterization of carbon nanotubes.
Define area for metal deposition for contacts.
Deposit Ti/Au 0.5 nm/50 nm for source-drain contacts in an e-beam evaporator chamber at 10-6 torr.
Leave the die in acetone overnight for metal liftoff.
Dip the die in IPA for 10 min and then blow dry using N2 gun.
Perform a blanket deposition of 500 nm e-beam evaporated SiO2 for gate dielectric at 10-6 torr.
Design a photomask for defining the gate electrode.
Follow steps 1.2-1.6 to define region for gate metal deposition.
Evaporate 50 nm/50 nm Cr/Au as the top gate electrode in e-beam evaporator.
Follow step 3.4 for metal liftoff.
Design a photomask to open a trench in SiO2 to access the carbon nanotube channel and design pad-etch area in the same mask.
Pattern the PR to open up the trench for wet etch of SiO2.
Wet etch the evaporated SiO2 using 1:20 BHF solution for 3 min and 30 sec.
Rinse the device in DI water thoroughly.
Dip the device in IPA for 5 min.
Blow dry the device using a N2 gun.
Prepare a solution of 6 mM 1-pyrenebutanoic acid succinimidyl ester (PBSE) in dimethylformamide (DMF).
Incubate the SWNT FET die in this linker molecular solution for 1 hr at room temperature.
Rinse the die in DMF to wash away excess reagent.
Blow-dry the device.
Prepare a 20 mg/ml solution of biotinyl-3,6-dioxaoctanediamine (BPA) in DI water for biotinylation of SWNTs.
Incubate the die in this BPA solution for 18 hours.
Thoroughly rinse the die in DI water and blow dry.
Prepare a solution of 1 mg/ml streptavidin in 7.2 pH PBS solution.
For static measurements, incubate the die in streptavidin solution for 20 minutes to completely functionalize the biotinylated SWNT.
Thoroughly rinse and blow dry the die after streptavidin binding.
Rinse the die by dispensing DI water (~50 ml) over the die using a squeeze bottle, then move the die to another Petri dish containing DI water and move it around for 1 minute.
Repeat the rinsing steps a total of 8-10 times.
Pour 9 parts by weight of PDMS monomer into a weighing cup.
Add 1 part by weight of curing agent to the PDMS monomer and thoroughly mix.
Degas the mixture in a desiccator for 25 minutes.
If foaming occurs during degassing, vent the chamber and let it settle down before continuing.
Pour the degassed PDMS mixture on top of a new silicon wafer in a Petri dish to create a PDMS layer of 5 mm above the wafer.
Place the Petri dish in an oven at 70 °C for 1 hour.
Remove the Petri dish from the oven and allow it to cool down.
Cut out a rectangular piece of PDMS using a scalpel.
Pull the cut-out PDMS piece out using tweezers.
Drill a hole with a 3 mm diameter biopsy punch from the flat side through to the other side of the PDMS piece.
Place the PDMS chamber on top of the device by aligning it over the active area of the SWNT FET dies.
Tap the PDMS gently to secure it onto the die.
Bond the flat side of the PDMS chamber to the die to ensure a leak-tight seal.
Remove the PDMS stamp after electrical testing and before chemical functionalization.
Dip the die in deionized water to help with removing the PDMS stamp.
Gently lift the PDMS stamp from the die.
Take a clean silicon wafer.
Place the silicon wafer on a hot plate at 200 °C for 5 minutes.
Spin coat SU-8 2015 at 500 rpm for 5 seconds.
Increase speed to 1,250 rpm and spin for 30 seconds.
Soft bake the wafer at 95 °C for 5 minutes.
Design a photomask to define the flow channel pattern on top of the SWNT area.
Expose the wafer to UV light (365 nm) for 0.9 seconds.
Post bake the die at 95 °C for 5 minutes.
Develop the pattern in SU-8 developer for 5 minutes with gentle shaking.
Rinse the wafer in IPA and blow dry with N2 gun.
Prepare a PDMS mixture following steps 5.1-5.2.
Place the wafer with SU-8 mold in a desiccator along with trichloro(3, 3, 3-trifluoropropyl)silane.
Turn on the vacuum pump and let the wafer sit under vacuum for 1 hour.
Pour degassed PDMS mixture onto the wafer and heat it at 70 °C for 1 hour.
Cut the PDMS mold using a scalpel.
Drill holes at each end of the flow channel with a biopsy punch (0.75 mm diameter).
Ensure to drill from the flat side to avoid rough edges.
Place the PDMS flow chamber on top of the device by aligning it with the active area of the fabricated SWNT FET dies under a microscope.
Tap the chamber gently to secure it in place.
Push a polyethylene tube into the holes and connect the other end to a fluid source and drain syringe.
Attach the syringe to a syringe pump system for controlled flow through the channel.
Connect the source and gate contacts of SWNT FET to voltage ports on a DAQ card.
Connect the drain contact of SWNT FET to an input port on the DAQ card through a current pre-amplifier.
Apply 30 millivolts (mV) to the source contact, sweep the gate voltage, and record the current from the drain.
For measurements in solution, keep the gate voltage sweep parameter within ±0.7 volts to avoid leakage and reactions between the gate metal electrode and solution.
Connect the Ref-out signal from a lock-in amplifier to the external modulation signal port on a frequency generator for AM modulated frequency output.
Connect the source contact of SWNT FET to the AM-modulated RF output port of the frequency generator using a bias tee.
Connect the gate contact of SWNT FET to a voltage port on the DAQ card.
Connect the drain contact to a lock-in amplifier.
Read the amplitude and phase of current through the DAQ input ports.
Hold source dc voltage at 0 volt.
Set AM signal frequency at 200 kHz.
Sweep the gate voltage while measuring the current from the drain.
Increase frequency and repeat the measurement for different frequencies.
Prepare 1 mM NaCl, 10 mM NaCl, and 100 mM NaCl salt solutions starting from a 5 M NaCl stock solution.
Take the SWNT device from step 3.13.
Carry out steps 4.1-4.5 to obtain a biotinylated device.
Place a PDMS chamber on top of the device.
Fill the chamber with DI water using a pipette.
Measure frequency mixing for different frequencies as in step 8.
Repeat measurements for 1 mM NaCl, 10 mM NaCl, and 100 mM NaCl solutions.
Withdraw previous solution from the chamber using a pipette.
Flush the chamber multiple times with new solution starting from low to high concentration.
Remove PDMS stamp by gently lifting it with tweezers.
Thoroughly rinse the device with DI water.
Carry out streptavidin binding as explained in steps 4.6-4.7.
Repeat steps 9.3 through 9.6 for real-time flow measurements.
Prepare a 100 mM NaCl salt solution starting from the 5 M NaCl stock solution.
Take the SWNT device from step 3.13.
Carry out steps 4.1-4.5 to obtain a biotinylated device.
Place the micro-fluidic flow channel on the device.
Connect an empty syringe to one end of the micro-fluidic channel for withdrawal mode operation.
Attach a syringe with background solution of 100 mM NaCl to the other end.
Set up the electrical measurement as detailed.
Fix the frequency at 10 MHz and gate voltage bias at 0 V.
Start the syringe pump in withdrawal mode (flow rate = 0.4 ml/hour).
Monitor the current signal with time.
Switch the solution to 1 mg/ml streptavidin in 100 mM NaCl.
Monitor the signal change for streptavidin-biotin binding.
